name: CHICAGO POKER
description: Chicago Poker is a Seven Card Stud variant where the pot is split between the highest poker hand and the player holding the highest (or lowest) spade in the hole. Face-up spades do not count—only concealed spades are eligible. This creates a unique dual-objective game where players must balance traditional poker hand strength with the hunt for hidden spades.

content.text: Chicago Poker is a Seven Card Stud variant where the pot is split between the highest poker hand and the player holding the highest (or lowest) spade in the hole. Face-up spades do not count—only concealed spades are eligible. This creates a unique dual-objective game where players must balance traditional poker hand strength with the hunt for hidden spades.

Chicago Poker emerged in American home games as a Seven Card Stud variant, likely in the mid-20th century. The game gained popularity as a 'Dealer's Choice' option due to its exciting split-pot mechanic and the added suspense of hunting for spades in the hole.
Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.
Seven Card Stud format: 2 cards face down, 4 cards face up, 1 card face down. Five betting rounds total.

items.text: Low Chicago: Pot splits between highest hand and LOWEST spade in the hole (Ace counts high). Best hole spade is 2♠, worst is A♠.
San Francisco: Same as Chicago but using Hearts instead of Spades. High San Francisco = highest heart in hole; Low San Francisco = lowest heart in hole.
Follow the Queen: When a Queen is dealt face up, the next card dealt becomes wild for all players, as do all other cards of that rank. If another Queen appears, the wild card changes.
Dirty Schultz: Similar to Follow the Queen, but wild cards are determined when any player shows a natural pair face up. The next card dealt becomes wild.
The Bitch: If the Queen of Spades is dealt face up, the hand ends immediately. Cards are reshuffled and redealt to players who hadn't folded.
Black Mariah: Multiple variants exist: sometimes synonymous with The Bitch, sometimes a version where you need both best hand AND highest spade to win.
